children: Ola Electric Mobility shares rose nearly 10 per cent in Wednesday's trading session, extending gains for the third straight day, amid positive sentiment following the launch of its new mass-market S1Z scooter range last month.

The rise also came amid a combination of developments around Ola Electric and the broader electric two-wheeler market, including the company's S1Z launch and a Rs 95.8-crore incentive sanctioned under the government's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.
The stock was quoted at Rs 41.50 per share on the NSE, up 9.85 per cent, at around 2:40 pm.
Nitant Darekar, Research Analyst at Bonanza, said the nearly 80 per cent rally from the March low of Rs 22.25 reflected a turnaround story rather than a recovery in earnings.

"Q1FY27 revenue fell 45 per cent YoY to Rs 455 crore but rose 72 per cent QoQ, as market share recovered to 8.4 per cent from 5.1 per cent. Gross margin held at 30.5 per cent despite commodity inflation," he said.
According to Darekar, key triggers include the Gigafactory expansion from 2.5 GWh towards 6 GWh, merchant cell sales and a Rs 1,500-crore fundraise enabling resolution.
"With an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 195 crore, breakeven depends on volumes continuing to grow," he said.
Shares of Ola Electric are up 77 per cent in the last six months, according to data available on BSE Analytics.
